question.:question/problem: Let $A$ be a $3\times 4$ matrix. If $B=\{{b}_{1}\}$ is a basis of $\text{Col}(A)$, find $\text{dim(Null}(A)).$
question.:question/worked-solution:
According to the rank-nullity theorem, if $A$ is a matrix with $n$ columns, then 

$$
\text{rank}(A)+\text{nullity}(A)=n.
$$

For the given matrix, we have $n=4,$ and since $B$ is formed by $1$ vectors, $\text{rank}(A)=1.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{rank}(A)+\text{nullity}(A) & =n \\ 1+\text{nullity}(A) & =4 \\ \text{nullity}(A) & =4-1 \\ \text{dim(Null}(A)) & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
According to the rank-nullity theorem, if $A$ is a matrix with $n$ columns, then 

$$
\text{rank}(A)+\text{nullity}(A)=n.
$$

For the given matrix, we have $n=9,$ and since $B$ is formed by $5$ vectors, $\text{rank}(A)=5.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{rank}(A)+\text{nullity}(A) & =n \\ 5+\text{nullity}(A) & =9 \\ \text{nullity}(A) & =9-5 \\ \text{dim(Null}(A)) & =4.\end{aligned}
$$
